mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing corporations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages by more than 1% in the same month signals a dual monetary-inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA +1% AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month MA +1% in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate, signals an overheating labor market that precedes a correction in equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA +3% AND UNRATE falls in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-month MA AND HOUST < 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
